title: Sky's recourse for bad debt is dilution and protocol seizure rather than a legal claim
content:
A.2.8.2.2.2.2.6 lists Sky's recourse for bad debt as "(1) minting Prime Agent tokens; (2) terminating a Prime's right to further borrowing; and (3) activation of the Resolution Mechanism which includes, without limitation, the authority to suspend all protocol operations, seize or reallocate all of the Prime assets, override or disable smart contract functions, initiate managed restructuring, or execute full and permanent liquidation of the affected sub-protocol and all of its assets."

Every remedy is executable by Sky directly. None requires a court, a counterparty's cooperation, or an enforceable legal judgment against an entity that may be offshore or pseudonymous — which is the usual weak point of lending into a decentralised ecosystem. The recourse works because Sky already holds the levers: the token override from the TGE makes minting possible, and control over the Prime's SubProxy and contracts makes seizure and override possible.

The escalation is well ordered. Minting recovers value from the Prime's equity holders without disturbing operations. Terminating borrowing stops the exposure growing. The Resolution Mechanism is the last resort and is deliberately total.

The stated purpose bounds it — "in order to contain risk and preserve the stability and solvency of the broader ecosystem" — but the powers are drafted expansively, "without limitation," and reach every asset of the sub-protocol.

Read with the conservatorship power over Prime Agents elsewhere in the Support Scope, a consistent principle emerges: Prime autonomy is real in operation and provisional in extremis, and the ecosystem always retains a unilateral path to recover its capital. The corollary for anyone holding a Prime's token is that they are junior to Sky's claim by design.
